rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reader should show tenderness and compassion to all creatures, honor the old, care for the young, and respect each creature’s right from its Creator.
rows.anchor: وارحم بني جميع الخلق كلهمو وانظر إليهم بعين اللطف والشفقة وقر كبير همو وارحم صغيرهمو

rows.speaker: الزروقي
rows.claim: All divine names may be emulated in their meanings except Allah, which calls for attachment alone; all names return to Him, so knowing Him entails knowing them.
rows.anchor: قال الزروقي رحمه الله كل الأسماء يصح التخلق بمعانيها إلا الاسم الله فإنه للتعلق فقط وكل الأسماء راجعة إليه

rows.speaker: الزروقي
rows.claim: The servant needs a singular heart with unalloyed unity and a singular secret, through which all aims are attained.
rows.anchor: ولا بد للعبد من قلب مفرد فيه توحيد مجرد وسر مفرد وبه يحصل جميع المقاصد

rows.speaker: الجنيد
rows.claim: Junayd says detachment from God’s distractions is reached through repentance that removes persistence, fear that removes delay, hope that prompts action, and humbling oneself before death.
rows.anchor: سئل الجنيد قدس سره كيف السبيل إلى الانقطاع

rows.speaker: الجنيد
rows.claim: Asked what enables this state, Junayd answers: a singular heart containing pure unity.
rows.anchor: قيل له بماذا يصل العبد إلى هذا قال : بقلب مفرد فيه توحيد مجرد

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The verse points to the comprehensive divine identity: unseen existence is named al-Bāṭin and manifest existence al-Ẓāhir.
rows.anchor: وفي التأويلات النجمية تشير الآية إلى هويته الجامعة عالم غيب الوجود المسمى باسم الباطن

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Al-Raḥmān is the general manifestation of mercy and al-Raḥīm its special manifestation; God transcends the distinction while manifesting both.
rows.anchor: هو الرحمن الرحيم أي هو المتجلي بالتجلي الرحماني العام وهو المتجلي بالتجلي الرحيمي الخاص

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Repeating huwa in the declaration of divine oneness emphasizes the importance of tawḥīd.
rows.anchor: كرر هو لإبراز الاعتناء بأمر التوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Malik means the possessor of sovereignty and command; the word also denotes governance through commands and prohibitions over people.
rows.anchor: فمعناه ذو الملك والسلطان والملك بالضم هو التصرف بالأمر والنهي في الجمهور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The governance sense applies specifically to rational people, hence one says king of people rather than king of things.
rows.anchor: وذلك يختص بسياسة الناطقين ولهذا يقال ملك الناس ولا يقال ملك الأشياء

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: The phrase King of the Day of Judgment means the King on that Day.
rows.anchor: كما في المفردات وعبد الملك هو الذي يملك نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A servant called ʿAbd al-Malik governs himself and others only as God wills and commands.
rows.anchor: وعبد الملك هو الذي يملك نفسه وغيره بالتصرف فيه بما شاء الله وأمره به

rows.speaker: الغزالي
rows.claim: Al-Ghazālī likens the servant’s private kingdom to heart and body, with desire, anger, and passion as troops and the limbs as subjects.
rows.anchor: قال الإمام الغزالي قدس سره مملكة العبد الخاصة به قلبه وقالبه وجنده شهوته وغضبه وهواه

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The pledge addresses the Prophet of the spirit and signifies believing souls entering under his spiritual law.
rows.anchor: وفي التأويلات النجمية قوله تعالى : يا أيها النبي

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The pledge against associating anything with God means that souls must not associate themselves with love of worldly life, desires, pleasures, adornments, and vanities.
rows.anchor: يبايعنك على أن لا يشركن بالله شيئا من حب الدنيا وشهواتها ولذاتها وزينتها

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The ban on theft means not borrowing the ego’s disobedient traits and blameworthy qualities.
rows.anchor: ولا يسرقن من أخلاق الهوى المتبع وصفاته الرديئة

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The ban on adultery means not joining and following the ego in its desires.
rows.anchor: ولا يزنين أي مع الهوى بالاتفاق معه والاتباع له

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The ban on killing children means not preventing or rejecting spiritual inspirations and divine thoughts.
rows.anchor: ولا يقتلن أولادهن أي لا يمنعن ولا يرددن أولاد الخواطر الروحانية

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The ban on fabricated slander forbids claiming visions, direct witnessing, detachment, asceticism, piety, trust, or surrender that one has not attained.
rows.anchor: ولا يأتين ببهتان يفترينه بين أيديهن وأرجلهن يعني لا يدعين بما لم يحصل لهن

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Obedience in what is right means following every moral trait and quality the spiritual guide commands.
rows.anchor: ولا يعصينك في معروف أي في كل ما تأمرهن من الأخلاق والأوصاف

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The guide accepts their sincere pledge and seeks forgiveness for earlier legal disobedience and natural conformity; God covers the former through legal conformity and shows mercy amid natural inclinations.
rows.anchor: فبايعهن أي فأقبل مبايعتهن بين يديك بالصدق والإخلاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here, taking people as allies means intimate alliance and affection.
rows.anchor: فالتولي هنا بمعنى الموالاة والموادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description of divine wrath and despair applies to unbelievers generally, since all are under wrath and lack the mercy of the afterlife.
rows.anchor: لأن كلهم مغضوب عليهم لا رحمة لهم من الرحمة الأخروية

rows.speaker: الأكثرون
rows.claim: Most commentators identify the people as Jews, citing its revelation about poor Muslims who allied with Jews to obtain their fruit.
rows.anchor: وقيل اليهود لما روي أنها نزلت في بعض فقراء المسلمين كانوا يواصلون اليهود ليصيبوا من ثمارهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qawm literally refers to men, but women may be included subordinately because the people of each prophet comprise men and women.
rows.anchor: والقوم الرجال وربما دخل النساء فيه على سبيل التبع لأن قوم كل نبي رجال ونساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the people are unbelievers generally, they despair of the afterlife through disbelief and lack of certainty in it.
rows.anchor: لكفرهم بها وعدم إيقانهم على أن يراد بقومه عامة الكفرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the referent is Jews, they despair of afterlife reward because they knowingly oppose the Torah-described Messenger despite his signs; they believe in resurrection but persist from envy and hostility.
rows.anchor: لعنادهم الرسول المنعوت في التوراة المؤيد بالآيات على أن يراد به اليهود

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet warned the Jewish community under oath that they knew he was truly God’s messenger and had brought truth, and urged them to accept Islam.
rows.anchor: قال عليه السلام : ما معشر اليهود ويلكم اتقوا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects al-Sajāwandī’s reading of the question as asking whether humans or others such as angels and believing jinn are better; it concerns whose deeds are better than others’.
rows.anchor: ولا معنى لقول السجاوندي في عين المعاني استفهام بمعنى الهمزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an’s attribution of goodness to human action means a person’s worth follows deeds: the best worker may look ugly, while the worst worker is the opposite.
rows.anchor: ولو أنه أبشع الناس منظر أو من كان عمله أسوأ كان بخلاف ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse says best, not most, because quantity has no value when the work is ugly.
rows.anchor: ولم يقل أكثر عملا لأنه لا عبرة بالكثرة مع القبح

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say goodness and badness are known through religious law: what the law approves is good and what it condemns is bad.
rows.anchor: قالوا والحسن إنما يدرك بالشرع فما حسنه الشرع فهو حسن

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another interpretation of the test is who takes better provision from life for death and gives more generously in this world for the next.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : ليبلوكم أيكم أحسن أخذا من حياته لموته وأحسن هبة

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet told ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar to use health before illness, youth before old age, free time before busyness, and life before death.
rows.anchor: قال النبي لعبد بن عمر رضي الله عنهما خذ من صحتك لسقمك ومن شبابك لهرمك

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Asked which believer is wisest, the Prophet answered: the one who remembers death most and prepares for it best.
rows.anchor: وسئل عليه السلام ، أي المؤمنين اكيس قال أكثرهم للموت ذكرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readiness for death and the afterlife means many sincere deeds, including prayer, fasting, alms, and pilgrimage.
rows.anchor: فالاستعداد للموت وللآخرة بكثرة الأعمال المقارنة للإخلاص سواء كانت صلاة أو صوما أو زكاة أو حجا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Deeds differ in merit: prayer is an ascent of witnessing that breaks the ego and tires the body, so earlier righteous people performed many cycles, reportedly up to a thousand nightly.
rows.anchor: كالصلاة فإنها معراج الشهود وفيها كسر النفس وإتعاب البدن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fasting and eating less bring divine wisdom to the heart and discipline character; some early ascetics fasted continuously for three to forty days, with forty said to open great wisdom.
rows.anchor: وكالصوم وتقليل الطعام فإنه سبب لورود الحكمة الإلهية إلى القلب ولذا كان بعض السلف يوصلون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers should race and hasten: the self is a mount, the world a track, and the foremost are brought near to God.
rows.anchor: فيا أيها المؤمنون سابقوا واسارعوا فالنفس مطية والدنيا مضمار والسابقون السابقون أولئك المقربون

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet says the spiritually singular have gone ahead; the author explains their singularity as severance from selves and horizons and witnessing the Real in absolute existence.
rows.anchor: وقد قال عليه السلام ، قد سبق المفردون والتفريد هو تقطيع الموحد عن الأنفس والآفاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Spiritual progress requires journeying and wayfaring, then flying in unity and divine singularity, leaving contingent lower realms for the realm of necessity and eternity.
rows.anchor: فلا بد من السير والسلوك ثم الطيران في هواء الوحدة ولهوية الذاتية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s might does not let the wrongdoer escape, while His forgiveness reaches those He wills through repentance and grace.
rows.anchor: لمن شاء منهم بالوبة وكذا بالفضل قال بعضهم

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One commentator says God’s pairing of might with forgiveness encourages sinners to repent rather than think their past makes them unfit for service.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم لما كان العزيز منا يهلك كل من خالفه إذا علم بمخالفته قال مرغبا للمسيء في التوبة

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A sacred report says God comes swiftly to one who approaches Him, reassuring the sinner who turns back.
rows.anchor: كما قال في الحديث القدسي ومن أتاني يمشي أتيته هرولة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God brought the seven heavens into existence without any prior model.
rows.anchor: أبدعها من غير مثال سبق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause is a resumption addressed to the Prophet or anyone fit to be addressed; calling it the creation of the Merciful instead of using a pronoun emphasizes powerful creation as mercy and grace, while min strengthens the negation.
rows.anchor: استئناف والخطاب للرسول أو لكل أحد ممن يصلح للخطاب ووضع خلق الرحمن موضع الضمير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavens show no inconsistency, disorder, or lack of proportion; their creation is upright and balanced.
rows.anchor: ما ترى فيه شيئا من اختلاف واضطراب في الخلقة وعدم تناسب بل هو مستو مستقيم

rows.speaker: القاشاني
rows.claim: Al-Qāshānī explains the absence of disparity by the heavens’ simplicity and roundness, matching layers, beautiful order, and proportion.
rows.anchor: قال القاشاني : سلب التفاوت عنها بساطتها واستدارتها ومطابقة بعضها بعضا

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib defines disparity as difference in qualities, each quality failing to match or fit the other.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب : التفاوت الاختلاف في الأوصاف كأنه يفوت وصف أحدهما الآخر

rows.speaker: بعض العلماء
rows.claim: Some scholars take creation generally; apparent opposites such as night and day are not defects, since nothing is needlessly excessive or deficient and all is balanced evidence of a knowing Creator.
rows.anchor: وجعل بعض العلماء خلق الرحمن عاما فسئل بأن المخلوقات بأسرها على غاية التفاوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ishārī reading sees universal raḥmānic mercy: upper and lower, luminous and dark, spiritual and bodily beings are created from the light and mercy of al-Raḥmān without disparity.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية إشارة إلى شمول رحمته الرحمانية الواسة كل شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An accompanying Persian couplet pictures the earth as a common table open to friend and foe, reinforcing the breadth of mercy.
rows.anchor: اديم زمين سفره عام اوست برين خوان يغماه دشمن ه دوست

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Return the gaze to the sky so observation makes the point clear and removes doubt; rajaʿa can be intransitive for returning or transitive for sending something back.
rows.anchor: أي رده إلى رؤية السماء حتى يتضح ذلك بالمعاينة ولا يبقى عندك شبهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Futūr is the plural of fatr and means a split or crack; the cited lexicon also gives the senses of creating, beginning, and splitting.
rows.anchor: جمع فطر كما في القاموس وهو الشق

rows.speaker: القاشاني
rows.claim: Al-Qāshānī says the sky has no cracks; openings would compromise the benefits arranged for the stars, and the created sky’s resistance to piercing points beyond the bodily realm of its Creator.
rows.anchor: قاله القاشاني : ولو كان لها فروج لفاتت المنافع التي رتبت لها النجوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to look twice means two further inspections, with the dual also expressing repeated and abundant looking rather than only two attempts.
rows.anchor: أي رجعتين أخريين وأعد النظر مرة بعد مرة في طلب الخلل والعيب

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says one could repeat the inspection until Judgment Day and still see no crack.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن رحمه الله لو كررته مرة بعد مرة إلى يوم القيامة لم تر فيه فطورا

rows.speaker: الواسطي
rows.claim: Al-Wāsiṭī interprets the two looks as the heart and the eye, since the first inspection used the eye alone.
rows.anchor: وقال الواسطي رحمه الله كرتين أي قلبا وبصرا لأن الأول كان بالعين خاصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeated looking and thinking establish facts; when searching for cracks yields only fatigue, the impossibility of finding them is confirmed.
rows.anchor: والحاصل أن تكرار النظر وتجوال الفكر مما يفيد تحقيق الحائق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The eye returns khāsiʾ, humbled and driven away from the fault it sought; the verb is parsed as a response to the commands and khāsiʾan as a circumstantial accusative.
rows.anchor: كأنه يطرد عن ذلك طرد بالصغار والذلة

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib connects khusūʾ of the eye with shrinking back in humiliation; the lexicons also describe the verb as being driven off or banished.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب ومنه خسأ البصر أي انقبض من مهانة وفي القاموس اخاسيء من الكلاب والخنازير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥasīr means exhausted and worn from the long, repeated inspection.
rows.anchor: أي كليل وبالاية الأعياء لطول المعاودة وكثرة لمراجعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Obtaining food, drink, and clothing involves many prior steps that a person could not manage alone.
rows.anchor: ومشروب وملبوس فيه مقدمات كثيرة لو احتاج العبد إلى مباشرتها بنفسه لعجز عن ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s way is to hide each subtle treasure inside something coarse: precious metals and gems in earth, pearls in shells, honey in bees, and silk in worms.
rows.anchor: ومن سنة الله سبحانه حفظ كل لطيفة في طي كل كثيفة كصيانة الودائع في المواضع المجهولة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heart, though a morsel of flesh, is the repository of knowledge and love of God and was created for this; the servant should cleanse it of attachment to anything else.
rows.anchor: وكذا جعل قلب العبد محلا ومعدنا لمعرفته ومحبته وهو مضغة لحم فالقلب خلق لهذا لا لغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is subtle and aware of what lies within, having placed the heart inside the body as a subtle gift.
rows.anchor: وصوف نفسه بأنه لطيف خبير مطلع على ما في الباطن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the heart is a site of divine beholding, empty it of distractions and fill it with knowledge, sciences, and mysteries, seeking manifestation through God’s names, attributes, and essence.
rows.anchor: ذا كان هو المنظر الإلهي وجب تخليته عن الأفكار والأغيار وتحليته بأنواع المعارف

rows.speaker: مكحول
rows.claim: Makḥūl estimates the inhabited world’s full extent as a 500-year journey: 200 years of sea, 200 uninhabited, 80 for Gog and Magog, and 20 for the rest of humanity.
rows.anchor: فروى عن مكحول إنه قال ما بين أقصى الدنيا إلى أدناها مسيرة خمسمائة سنة مائتان من ذلك في البحر

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda estimates the world’s circumference at 24,000 farsakhs, divided among Sudanese lands (12,000), Romans (8,000), Persians and Turks (3,000), and Arabs (1,000).
rows.anchor: وعن قتادة إنه قال الدنيا إن بسيطها من حيث يحيط بها البحر المحيط أربعة وعشرون ألف فرسخ

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar says the Sudanese who do not wear clothes are more numerous than all other people combined.
rows.anchor: وعن عبد الله بن عمر رضي الله عنهما ، إنه قال : ربع من لا يلبس الثياب من السودان

rows.speaker: بطليموس
rows.claim: Ptolemy gives the earth’s circumference, diameter, and area, and converts among stadia, miles, farsakhs, cubits, spans, fingers, and barleycorns; the text preserves his measurements as estimates.
rows.anchor: وقد خرج بطليموس مقدار قطر الأرض واستدارتها في المجطي بالتقريب

rows.speaker: صاحب الخريدة
rows.claim: The author of al-Kharīda says Ptolemy’s figures, if true, are revelation or inspiration, and if inferred by measurement are still near the truth; Makḥūl’s and Qatāda’s figures do not yield certain knowledge of the unseen.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب الخريدة فإن كان ذلك حقا فهو وحي من الحق أو إلهام وإن كان قياسا واستدلالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhālūl means very soft and compliant, making travel easy so people can reach what benefits them.
rows.anchor: أي لينة منقادة اية الانقياد لما تفهمه صيغة المبالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhill with ḍamma means ease or submissiveness, while dhull with ḍamma means humiliation; dhālūl is an active faʿūl form and lacks feminine marking despite the feminine noun earth.
rows.anchor: وجعل صاحبا لقاموس الذل ضد الصعوبة بالضم والكسر والذل بمعنى الهوان بالضم فقط والذلول فعول بمعنى الفاعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to walk follows from the earth’s being made compliant; some take it as permission, while others read it as a report phrased as a command.
rows.anchor: أي فاسلكوا في جوانبها وخبر في صورة الأمر عند آخرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Manākib may mean the earth’s sides, likened to a man’s shoulders; walking its edges gives access to its benefits.
rows.anchor: من حيث أي منكبي الرجل جانباه فشبه الجوانب بالمناكب وإذا مشوا وساروا في جوانبها وأطرافها

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib defines a mankib as the joint between upper arm and shoulder and explains its metaphorical use for the earth, as in the expression its back.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب المنكب مجتمع ما بين العضد والكتف ومنه استعير للأرض في قوله فامشوا في مناكبها

rows.speaker: بشر بن كعب
rows.claim: When Bushr ibn Kaʿb made a captive woman’s freedom depend on naming the earth’s shoulders, she answered that they were its mountains; later, when he sought to marry her, Abū al-Dardāʾ advised him to leave what troubled him.
rows.anchor: وكان لبشر بن كعب سرية فقال لها أن أخبرتني ما مناكب الأرض فأنت حرة فقالت مناكبها جبالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the mountains the earth’s shoulders works because raised terrain fits the image; if people can walk the mountains, the earth is thoroughly subdued, while rare inaccessible mountains do not overturn the general claim.
rows.anchor: فإذا جعل الأرض في الذل بحيث يتأتى المشي في مناكبها لم يبق منها شيء لم يتذلل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wall separating people from Gog and Magog is said to be slippery and difficult to cross; such exceptional mountains are not considered because they are rare.
rows.anchor: ورد في الحدي إنه تزالق عليه الأرجل ولا تثبت ومنها ما يشق سلوكها

rows.speaker: السعدي المفتي
rows.claim: Al-Saʿdī al-Muftī says the camel analogy means subduing it to the utmost, since its shoulder is too thin and raised for a rider to tread on.
rows.anchor: كما في حواشي سعدي المفتي فإن منكب البعير أرق أعضائه وأنباها

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The inner reading makes the earth of human nature compliant: take only needed, legally permitted bodily pleasures to strengthen the body and prepare for worship.
rows.anchor: فوي التأويلات النجمية : هو الذي جعل لكم أرض البشرية ذلولا منقادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If eat is an imperative of permission, provision means lawful food; if it is a report in command form, the provision can include prohibited food even though consuming it is forbidden.
rows.anchor: يكون شاملا للحرام أيضا فإنه من رزقه أيضا وإن كان التناول منه حراما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Resurrection is the return to God after being raised; the verse calls for abundant gratitude for His blessing, and the verb nashara may be transitive or intransitive.
rows.anchor: أي المرجع بعد البعث فبالغوا في شكر عمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A-amintum is a rebuking question; the first hamza is interrogative, the second belongs to the verb, and man is a relative pronoun.
rows.anchor: وهو استفهام توبيخ فالهمزة الألوى استفهامية والثانية من نفس الكلمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those in heaven may mean angels managing the world, or God with His command and decree in heaven; this resembles the statement that He is God in the heavens and earth.
rows.anchor: أي الملائكة الموكلين بتدبير هذا العالم أو الله سبحانه على تأويل من في السماء أمره وقضاؤه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Heaven is singled out to show that earthly idols are not gods; the divine elevation means power and sovereignty, not location or bodily direction.
rows.anchor: خص السماء بالذكر ليعلم إن الأصنام التي في الأرض ليست بآلهة لا لأنه تعالى في جهة من الجهات

rows.speaker: الشعراني
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿrānī says belief in divine elevation does not entail direction; hands are raised in prayer because heaven is a place of blessings and the prayer direction, while God is the heart’s direction.
rows.anchor: كما في الكبريت الأحمر للإمام الشعراني قدس سره وإما رفع الأيدي إلى السماء في الدعاء فلكونها محل البركات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the wording may reflect the Arabs’ claim that God is in heaven, while affirming that He transcends place.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون الظرفية باعتبار زعم العرب حيث كانوا يزعمون إنه تعالى في السماء

rows.speaker: فتح الرحمن
rows.claim: Fatḥ al-Raḥmān treats this passage as an ambiguous verse whose meaning God has reserved; believers affirm it and entrust its interpretation to Him.
rows.anchor: وفي فتح الرحمن هذا المحل من المتشابه الذي استأثر الله بعلمه ونؤمن به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is parsed as asking whether people feel secure from the One in heaven making the earth swallow them after they disbelieved in the gift of a subdued earth.
rows.anchor: قوله من في السماء في موضع النصب على أنه مفعول أمنتم أن يخسف بكم الأرض

rows.speaker: الجوهري
rows.claim: Al-Jawharī explains khusūf as sinking into the earth; the construction with bā makes God cause someone to disappear into it.
rows.anchor: قال الجوهري خسف المكان يخسف خسوفا ذهب في الأرض وخسف الله به الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the threat that the earth will swallow people, bā marks accompaniment or causation, meaning that the earth covers them as they are made to disappear within it.
rows.anchor: والمشهور إن الباء في مثل هذا الموضع للتعدية أي يدخلكم ويذهبكم فيها

rows.speaker: القاموس
rows.claim: Al-Qāmūs likewise defines the expression as God making a person vanish inside the earth.
rows.anchor: وفي القاموس أيضا خسف الله بفلان الأرض غيبه فيها

rows.speaker: القاموس
rows.claim: Mawr means agitation, flowing over the earth, and movement; the earth would move back and forth instead of remaining subdued and still.
rows.anchor: قال في القاموس المور الاضطراب والجريان على وجه الأرض والتحرك أي تضطرب ذهابا ومجيئا

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One interpretation says the earth will revolve with its inhabitants toward the lower earth.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم فإذا الأرض تدور بكم إلى الأرض السفلى

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another interpretation says the earth opens so people fall into it, closes, then opens again to punish them.
rows.anchor: وبعضهم تنكشف تارة للخوض فيها وتلتئم أخرى للتعذيب بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second threat asks whether people are secure from a hail of stones sent from heaven, as happened to Lot’s people and the people of the Elephant; there is no safety from either threat while they persist in idolatry.
rows.anchor: أي حجارة من السماء كما أرسلها على قوم لوط وأصحاب الفيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the threatened punishment arrives, people will know God’s warning is true and severe, but that knowledge will no longer benefit them or help avert it.
rows.anchor: أي إنذاري عند مشاهتدكم للمنذر به أهو واقع أم لا أشديد أم ضعيف

rows.speaker: برهان القرآن
rows.claim: Burhān al-Qurʾān says the earth-swallowing threat comes first because people live on earth, which is nearer, then the hail threat comes from heaven.
rows.anchor: قال في برهان القرآن خوفهم بالخسف أولا لكونهم على الأرض وإنها أقرب إليهم من السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inner reading compares heedless people’s remaining under blankets instead of rising for dawn prayer to being swallowed by the earth, while a saint’s wakefulness is a blessing and nakedness is a lesser trial than heedlessness.
rows.anchor: أشارت الآية الأولى على ما ألهمت في جوف الليل إلى إن الاستتار تحت اللحاف وعدم النهوض إلى الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A saint who rose for night worship, shivered, and wept at being unclothed was told that being awakened was a gift and others’ sleep a punishment; he should be grateful.
rows.anchor: قيل له من قبل الله تعالى أقمناك وانمناهم فتبكى علينا يعين إن إقامتك وإنامة الغافلين نعمة لك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inner reading treats heavy rain as wrath disguised as mercy when it keeps a worshipper from night prayer or purification; one should seize free time before busyness.
rows.anchor: واشارت الآية الثانية إلى نزول المطر الشديد من السماء فإه ربما يمنع المتهجد عن القيام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat recalls earlier deniers such as Noah’s and ʿĀd’s peoples; the shift to third person signals turning away, and their punishment was terrifying, consoling the Prophet and threatening his people.
rows.anchor: أي من قبل كفار مكة من كفار الأمم السالفة كقوم نوح وعاد وأضرابهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vision is physical sight because the verb takes ilā; inward vision would take fī.
rows.anchor: فالرؤية بصرية لأنها تتعدى بإلى وإما القلبية فتعديتها بفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ṭayr can be a generic singular for winged creatures that fly, either a plural form used as a genus or a verbal noun; al-Mufradāt calls it the plural of ṭāʾir.
rows.anchor: والطير يطلق على جنس الطائر وهو كل ذي جناح يسبح في الهواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fawqahum may modify the act of seeing or describe the birds as being above the observers.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون ظرفا ليروا وأن يكون حالا من الطير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saffāt describes birds with wings spread in flight, while yaqbiḍna describes their wings folding occasionally to beat against the air; qudām are the forward feathers of a wing.
rows.anchor: وكذا يقبضن إنما هو أجنحة الطير لا أنفسها والمعنى باسطات أجنحتهم في الجو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The present tense yaqbiḍna signals repeated folding; as in swimming, birds’ basic motion is extending and spreading, with occasional folding to propel themselves.
rows.anchor: وهو الشر في إيثار يقبضن الدال على تجدد القبض تارة بعد تارة على قابضات

rows.speaker: ابن الشيخ
rows.claim: Ibn al-Shaykh says yaqbiḍna is coordinated with the noun saffāt because it means and folding; otherwise a verb could not be coordinated with a noun.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الشيخ ويقبضن عطف على صافات لأنه بمعنى وقابضات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone keeps the birds aloft and prevents their fall, contrary to the downward pull of their bodily nature.
rows.anchor: في الجو وما يأخذهن عن السقوط عند الصف والقبض على خلاف مقتضى الطبع الجسماني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Merciful’s encompassing mercy creates birds with forms and properties suited to moving through air.
rows.anchor: الواسع رحمته كل شيء بأن برأهن على أشكال وخصائص وهيأهن للجري في الهواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s sight reveals visible things, even what lies beneath the earth; the author says sight is an attribute additional to knowledge, contrary to the Qadariyya.
rows.anchor: لا يعزب عنه ما تحت الثرى وهو في حقه تعالى عبارة عن الوصف الذي به ينكشف كال نعوت المبصرات فالبصر صفة زائدة على علمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fruit of faith in this attribute is constant self-watchfulness and exact moral accounting.
rows.anchor: فمن عرف هذه الصفة كان المراد به دوام المرقابة ومطالبة النفس بدقيق المحاسة
